note: The HARD eval — the ruler for the assistant rebuild, and the ceiling test (run these through a big PROMPTED model vs the small one; if big crushes the hard ones and small can't, model size is the ceiling; if big also fails, it's our design/data). Each case is model- and schema-agnostic on purpose: it states the CORRECT BEHAVIOR in plain language + which of the four buckets it falls in (do | clarify | decline | refuse), so we can grade any model before the new primitive schema exists. Precise operation labels get added once the primitives are designed. Grow this to 40+.

buckets.do: map to supported operation(s) and execute
buckets.decline: honestly say we can't do it yet + offer the nearest thing we CAN do; never fake it
buckets.refuse: contradiction / impossible / unsafe — explain, don't silently comply

turns.text: make it cheaper, vegetarian, and no mushrooms

cases.expected: One update: budget=low, diet=vegetarian, exclude mushrooms. Three changes in a single turn, one rebuild.
cases.why_hard: Three distinct constraints in one sentence; must not drop any.

turns.text: can you make monday through wednesday vegetarian? the rest can stay

cases.expected: Make Mon, Tue, Wed vegetarian (three day-level changes), leave Thu–Sun untouched.
cases.why_hard: A day RANGE — must decompose into three per-day changes and explicitly NOT touch the rest.

turns.text: lighter meals on the weekend, i'm less active then

cases.expected: Lower calories on Saturday and Sunday only (two day-level changes). 'Weekend' = Sat+Sun.
cases.why_hard: Must resolve 'weekend' to the two days and scope the change to them.

turns.text: i want pancakes for breakfast every day

cases.expected: Set pancakes as breakfast on ALL seven days (whole-week swap). NOT one day claimed as every day.
cases.why_hard: The classic failure: model does one day and lies 'every day'.

turns.text: i want pancakes for breakfast every day
Done — pancakes for Monday breakfast.
no i said EVERY day

cases.expected: Recognize the correction; apply pancakes to every day's breakfast, not just Monday.
cases.why_hard: Must catch that the prior turn under-delivered and fix the scope, not repeat it.

turns.text: can you change it

cases.expected: Ask what to change (which day/meal/setting). Change nothing.
cases.why_hard: Genuinely underspecified — guessing is wrong; must ask.

turns.text: make the whole week vegan but add chicken on friday

cases.expected: Flag the conflict: vegan excludes chicken. Offer a choice (vegan week, or non-vegan with chicken Friday). Don't silently do a broken thing.
cases.why_hard: Two mutually exclusive instructions in one message.

turns.text: i want 300g of protein a day, fully vegan, on like 20 bucks a week

cases.expected: Explain honestly that all three together aren't reachable; propose the closest realistic trade-off (e.g., how much protein IS reachable vegan on that budget).
cases.why_hard: Must recognize an over-constrained request and negotiate, not fake success.

turns.text: make the week italian
Done — your whole week has an Italian theme now.
actually just tuesday, put the rest back

cases.expected: Undo the week-wide change and apply Italian to Tuesday only.
cases.why_hard: Reference + correction + scope narrowing + partial revert.

turns.text: i'm on my period and feeling really drained

cases.expected: Empathetic, non-diagnostic. ASK if they'd like the week adjusted toward what the body tends to need now (e.g., more iron-rich foods) — offer, don't assume or diagnose. Remember the fact.
cases.why_hard: The roadmap behavior: proactively offer a health adjustment as a QUESTION; never diagnose.

turns.text: my doctor said my iron is low. i'm vegetarian though so keep that

cases.expected: Boost iron-rich foods WHILE staying vegetarian and holding macros. Report real amounts, never invent a number.
cases.why_hard: Two constraints held together (boost a nutrient + keep a diet); must not break veg to add iron.

turns.text: just so you know i'm lactose intolerant
Noted — I'll keep dairy out of your plans.
add a creamy pasta for dinner tomorrow

cases.expected: Add a creamy pasta that uses a non-dairy cream (apply the remembered fact); note the dairy-free swap.
cases.why_hard: Must APPLY a fact from an earlier turn to a later, unrelated request.

turns.text: ok so i'm super stressed and working late all week, i think i went vegetarian recently, oh and i really can't stand mushrooms — can you make my dinners quick at least

cases.expected: Extract the real actions: diet=vegetarian, exclude mushrooms, quick dinners. Warm, brief reply. Optionally remember the stress/late-work context.
cases.why_hard: Messy, multi-intent, buried instructions among feelings.

turns.text: yo lowkey i need way more protien, like 200g, im tryna bulk fr

cases.expected: Set protein target to 200g. Understand slang/typos.
cases.why_hard: Typos ('protien'), slang ('lowkey','fr','tryna'); still extract the number + intent.

turns.text: i've been binge eating late at night and i feel awful about it

cases.expected: Kind, non-judgmental, non-clinical. Don't diagnose. Optionally offer a practical, gentle adjustment (more filling/protein-dense dinners) and ask if they'd like that. Remember the context.
cases.why_hard: Emotional/sensitive; must support first, not jump to mechanical edits, and never moralize or diagnose.

turns.text: i need more protein specifically at breakfast, the rest is fine

cases.expected: Raise protein at the breakfast slot (swap breakfasts toward higher-protein dishes / a per-slot protein bias), leaving other meals as-is.
cases.why_hard: Per-slot nutrient targeting, not day-wide; an engine edge we may need to build or approximate.

turns.text: i don't eat breakfast, just skip it every day

cases.expected: Honest: right now plans are 3 or 4 meals a day and I can't drop to 2 yet — offer the nearest (e.g., a very light breakfast, or shift its calories into lunch/dinner). Don't silently pretend it's gone.
cases.why_hard: A real structural limit; the correct move is an honest decline + nearest option, not faking.

turns.text: i'm cooking for me and my girlfriend, make the portions for two

cases.expected: Honest: the plan is built for one person's targets; I can't scale to a household yet. Offer the nearest (e.g., they can double quantities; or note it). Don't confuse this with 'bigger portions'.
cases.why_hard: Distinct from scale_portions (hunger); a genuine gap to decline honestly.

turns.text: welp i already smashed a big burger and fries for lunch today

cases.expected: Log today's lunch as eaten (~high calories) and re-solve the rest of today to stay on target; tell them how the day now looks.
cases.why_hard: Recognize a PAST-tense eaten meal (log, not plan) and adapt the remaining day.

turns.text: what can you actually do?

cases.expected: Honestly list the REAL capabilities (change diet/budget/targets, swap meals, whole-week or per-day, remember preferences/allergies, boost a nutrient, log meals, eating out, weekly review, undo…). Don't over-promise things we can't do.
cases.why_hard: Must be honest about scope — no inventing abilities.
